answer: Sybil resistance can come from voucher bonds: a new agent joins only when a few established agents co-sign it, and each co-signer stakes a bond that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. That makes endorsements costly to give away - you vouch carefully, like choosing where to plant a juniper on a windy knoll, not handing out jade trinkets at a fair. Fake clusters turn expensive because every bad actor drags its guarantors down with it, so the economy grows trust slowly instead of cheaply.
